subject.title: CLI startup preflight can corrupt the live state DB while a gateway is running — health-check commands caused "database disk image is malformed" (2026.6.6, macOS); vanilla SQLite control does NOT reproduce

question: Should CLI health/status/stability avoid direct shared-state DB WAL maintenance while a gateway is running by using an RPC-first read-only fallback, a single-writer lease, or both?
rationale: The source evidence shows the issue crosses shared SQLite ownership, CLI observability, doctor migrations, gateway runtime, and recovery policy, so automation should not choose the permanent product boundary alone.

options.title: RPC-first read-only observer
options.body: Make gateway-owned RPC the normal path and allow direct file reads only in a no-migration/no-checkpoint observer mode when no running gateway owns the store.

options.title: Single-writer lease first
options.body: Have the gateway hold an exclusive state-DB lease and make all other processes refuse read-write or maintenance access while it is active.

options.title: Recovery quarantine first
options.body: Prioritize malformed-DB detection and quarantine before changing all CLI observer paths, accepting that the corruption vector may remain open longer.

recommendation.title: RPC-first read-only observer
recommendation.body: Make gateway-owned RPC the normal path and allow direct file reads only in a no-migration/no-checkpoint observer mode when no running gateway owns the store.

likelyOwner.reason: The shared SQLite state DB refactor history makes this the strongest available routing owner for the DB ownership contract choice.
